newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end up on lunar new year demand.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end up on lunar new year demand.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed higher on Wednesday as demand for liquidity began rising with companies preparing for bonus payments before the Chinese lunar new year on February 7, brokers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 5.459 percent against Tuesday's 5.350 close, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.50 percent against 5.25-5.30.
Dealers expected the rates to stabilise with Thursday's scheduled maturation of T$10 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit.
In the bond market, the seven-year 86/3 bond yield was at 5.9450 against 5.9600 and the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.1450 against 6.1475.
